- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.11 and price rises), especially in early forecast periods.
- Underestimate price declines following negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.22), particularly when recent prices are high.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% when sentiment swings are sharp.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward; if below, adjust upward — especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in 3–5 consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently 2–4% too high in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 2–3% for first 7 days of forecast horizon.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is consistently positive (0.11+), model tends to overestimate; when negative (–0.22–), underestimates — adjust forecast by ±1–2% based on sentiment magnitude.
